notes: Sports covers physics-based athletics, and this is one: an Olympics-style score attack whose formal scoring is altitude, airtime, top speed, grind distance and flips. It was a close call - Infinite Runner owns the endless recycled world and the one-more-run framing, so it is named second and lends the horizon occlusion and the cleanup volume behind the camera that the author's recycling answer needs, but it cannot lead, because its own boundary rule is that forward motion is automatic and here the player generates every bit of momentum; Racing was rejected for having no lap or finish line and Simulation's Physics Sim for being ramps and ragdoll contraptions rather than open water. No catalogue shape fits, so the shape is described - an endless stylized ocean with gentle rolling waves, played as a volume both above and below one continuous water surface that the dolphin swims under, hydroplanes along and launches off - and the rejections are specific: volume-open-air is open air with discrete touch-down surfaces "instead of one continuous ground plane", which is exactly what this is not; space-bounded assumes a bounded single-level space and the ocean is explicitly unbounded; world-open promises a contiguous map explored for its places, and there are no places in it; interior-endless has the endlessness but is enclosed. Decided without a user: the axes are all default except play-space, which is volumetric because play runs through the water column and the air above it, so the route is CHECK rather than P0 - the check should clear, since the volume is a play-height envelope over a single water plane and never self-occludes; the drawn extent is the author's roughly 500 studs in each direction fading into the horizon and recycling with the camera, no preset in either loaded file matches a trick-run ocean, and camera, controls, spray and combo scoring are mechanics rather than layout.
